sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section discusses the change in which month is considered first, from Tishrei before the Giving of the Torah to Nissan afterward, based on Targum Yonasan.

translations.translation: "This month is for you the head of the months, it is the first for you of the months of the year."
And the Rebbe, my father-in-law, the Rebbe, brings in his maamar beginning with these words
(at the beginning of his arrival in the USA)
that it is stated in Targum Yonasan on the verse
"In the month of the strong ones etc., it is the seventh month"
(which refers to the month of Tishrei),
"The ancients called it the first month etc., and now it is the seventh month,"
that before the Giving of the Torah
Tishrei was called the first month because in it the world was created,
and now,
after the Exodus from Egypt and the Giving of the Torah,
Nissan is the first month and Tishrei is the seventh month.
And he clarifies in this,
that since initially Tishrei was the first month, why was it changed so that Nissan should be the first.
And if it is because of the redemption that was in Nissan,
this itself requires explanation,
for the beginning of the redemption was in Tishrei,
for on Rosh HaShanah
(the first of Tishrei)
the servitude ceased for our forefathers,
and why is the month of the redemption
(the complete one)
specifically Nissan.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that Tishrei is the source of natural vitality for the year, while Nissan is the head for the miraculous, transcendent divine flow.

translations.translation: B)
And it should be noted,
that in several discourses
the precision in this—that Nissan is the head of the months—is in that the first of Tishrei is Rosh HaShanah
(that this, that the first of Tishrei is Rosh HaShanah, is also now after the Exodus from Egypt and the Giving of the Torah),
for since that which is called Rosh HaShanah is
because it includes the vitality of the entire year, analogous to the head which includes the vitality of all the limbs of the body,
and it is then divided into twelve heads of months, and each Rosh Chodesh into thirty
(twenty-nine)
days,
it is therefore found that the vitality of the month of Nissan is from Tishrei,
and here it is stated that Nissan is the head of the months and the first of the months of the year
(even to the month of Tishrei).
And they explain in this,
that the vitality drawn down in Tishrei for the entire year is in the aspect of boundary and measure
(which, in general, is the vitality that is clothed within the creations in their inwardness),
which is the root of the conduct of nature.
And this, that Nissan is called "head," is regarding the drawing down of the light of Ein Sof, blessed be He,
which is the root of miraculous conduct that is above nature.
And based on this they explain
also this, that Tishrei is Rosh HaShanah and Nissan is the head of the months,
for the conduct of nature,
which is always uniform,
is analogous to the course of the sun
(shanah [year] from the word shinui [change/repetition],
that the same thing returns and is repeated again),
and miraculous conduct, whose essence is renewal
[that sometimes the Holy One, blessed be He, disrupts the conduct of nature for a period of time],
is analogous to the course of the moon,
which is renewed each month
(chodesh [month] from the word chiddush [renewal]).
And it can be said,
that this which is precise in this maamar—that before the Exodus from Egypt Tishrei was the first of the months—
the emphasis in this is,
that before the Exodus from Egypt Tishrei was the first and the head also for the drawing down of Divinity that is above nature
[and this is also understood from that which even the beginning of the redemption of the Exodus from Egypt was in Tishrei],
so why was it changed now that Nissan is the first.
